_comment: The maintainer's M4 Mac mini, kept as the record behind docs/PHASE1_RESULTS.md.
Use it with --scenarios scripts/bench/scenarios.m4.json. It is refused on any
other platform: its sizes and contexts describe this machine.
Nothing here is guessed from your machine: model names, sizes and the
contexts that do or do not fit are things only you know, and a harness
that assumed them would induce the wrong condition and report a pass.
Sizes are the resident footprint in GB, which is weights plus KV cache at
the context you run them at, not the file size /api/tags reports. Read
them off `ollama ps` while the model is loaded.
Run the harness against a runtime you control. Both scripts load and
unload models.

host.label: M4 Mac mini, 16 GB unified
host.notes: iogpu.wired_limit_mb reads 0 on this M4, so the agent falls back to 75% of total RAM.

_comment: resident_gb above is measured at `fits`. The footprint is weights plus
KV cache and the second grows fast — the 4B model measured 3.4 GB at
8192 and 7.96 GB at 131072 on this host — so a pair that fits at a
small context stops fitting at a large one. That is what makes
eviction inducible on a machine with room for both models.
For the reference controller. Workflow A holds `held` continuously.
Workflow B's step may run on any model in `acceptable`, in preference
order — the operator declares that, not Wicklee. `defer_allowed` lets
the wicklee policy wait rather than displace.
